static_traits.name: Lin Lan
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy in the past; has had similar anxiety and catastrophizing in work-related situations before.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to identify and describe own thought patterns; steady tone but marked anxiety in the chief complaint; tending to overanalyze others' words.

basic_info.main_problem: I often catastrophize, causing anxiety and stress. For example, this afternoon my boss scheduled a meeting with me, and my first reaction was that he thinks I'm not performing well and wants to put me on probation. These anxious and catastrophic thoughts have existed since I can remember, and have become more pronounced in recent months. I tend to expect the worst, overanalyze, and jump to conclusions, especially at work, frequently before meetings or when receiving feedback.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent anxiety and stress have started affecting my work performance and overall well-being, so I hope to improve through counseling.
growth_experiences: Long-standing (since I can remember) frequent catastrophizing and anxiety thinking patterns in work-related situations; in the past often coped in similar situations by 'working harder to prove myself'; has not yet received psychotherapy, and has no significant physical illness.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / I may be a failure

special_situations.event: The boss scheduling an afternoon meeting on the same day
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the boss suddenly schedules a meeting, it usually means I am underperforming and may be disciplined or put on probation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Working doubly hard to prove myself, and over-preparing and worrying before meetings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He thinks I am not doing well and may put me on probation

special_situations.event: Receiving performance or daily feedback at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others give me feedback, it often means they are dissatisfied with me or negating me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-analyzes others' words and expressions, looking for negative signs
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are not satisfied with my performance

special_situations.event: A meeting is approaching; needing to discuss work matters in front of colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my work is discussed in front of colleagues, I will make a fool of myself and be seen as a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Worrying in advance, rehearsing the worst case to try to avoid losing control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I'll embarrass myself in front of everyone; everyone will think I am a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, fairly evaluated, and to have stable job security
core_conflict.fear: Fears being criticized or humiliated and defined as a failure, thereby affecting work and interpersonal relations
defense_goal: Reducing uncertainty and risk through overexertion and pre-emptively anticipating the worst
Maintains high sensitivity to others' evaluations to avoid 'mistakes'

object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges or superiors who may impose sanctions

object_relations.self_representation: A person who will be seen as a failure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (such as a supervisor or the counselor) discuss her work performance, arrange a meeting, or offer feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing the other as a harsh judge, subconsciously believing they are dissatisfied and may humiliate me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently pointing out the conjecture in a supportive tone, inviting evidence and concretization of the situation; using open-ended questions, reducing confrontation, helping differentiate facts from assumptions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing possible negative consequences or uncertain situations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Using abstract reasoning and overanalysis to control uncertainty, avoiding directly feeling anxiety and vulnerability
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Guiding attention to present experience and body sensations, slowing speech, replacing abstract reasoning with concrete facts; taking on the anxiety with an empathic tone before reality-testing.

positive_force: Received positive evaluation from the boss last quarter; colleagues often seek their help, positive feedback from others exists
Having self-regulation strategies like deep breathing and mindfulness that can ease anxiety briefly
Willing to actively seek counseling, positive attitude and willing to practice thought reframing
Higher education level; has professional ability and a work foundation
negative_force: Catastrophizing, jumping to conclusions (mind reading and predicting the future), overgeneralizing, and personalizing cognitive tendencies
Sustained worry about worst outcomes causing sleep disturbance
Over-analyzes others' words and feedback, highly sensitive to evaluation
Long-term work-related anxiety affecting work performance and colleague relationships

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing in work situations accompanied by intense anxiety
antecedent: Boss arranging a meeting at short notice
target_behavior.core_reason: High sensitivity to negative evaluation and catastrophic cognitive patterns (mind reading, predicting the future, overgeneralization, and personalization)
target_behavior.function: Escapes potential failure and humiliation to seek safety and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance affected, interpersonal relationships damaged, sleep disrupted by persistent worry, overall decline in sense of well-being
